E1.evidence: Reporter gives a reproducer (`const auto negative_ns = rclcpp::Time(-1);` vs `rclcpp::Time(-1, 0)`) and the log showing only the second throws: "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'\n  what():  cannot store a negative time point in rclcpp::Time"; merged fix ros2/rclcpp#2510 (https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/issues/2507).

E2.evidence: The defect is an inconsistency between two constructors of the same class inside rclcpp: the (int32_t seconds, uint32_t nanoseconds) constructor rejects negative time, the (int64_t nanoseconds) constructor does not. PR #2510: "rclcpp::Time currently allows a negative time when constructing with int64_t nanoseconds (but not with int32_t seconds even though both can possibly hold a negative value)." The fix adds `if (nanoseconds < 0) { throw std::runtime_error("cannot store a negative time point in rclcpp::Time"); }` inside rclcpp's own time.cpp. The behaviour is the same for any caller; no value, frame, unit, name, or timing crosses a boundary between two separately deployable units in a way that depends on a mutual assumption. The only 'second unit' is a test program invoking the API.

E3.evidence: Not evaluated beyond E2: there is no failing composition of two units; the reporter's program only calls the library constructor.

E4.evidence: The missing check is observed: "`negative_ns` does not throw, only `negative_s_ns` does" (https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/issues/2507).

The fix also adds negative-result checks to operator+= and operator-= and removes tests that allowed negative rclcpp::Time. A behaviour change that could affect downstream callers (API contract tightening) is a consequence of the fix, not a documented failed interaction.
